title: The Onion’s Latest Joke: Taking Over Infowars

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收看《重构者》，这是一个充满对设计的热爱以及探讨其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着30万个最珍爱的藏品去上班，把DJ台变成一个由美丽的50年历史老物件组成的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听来自奥彼（Audemars Piguet）的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是蕾切尔·亚当斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: This is not a joke.
sentences.zh: 这不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: The satirical outlet The Onion is set to take over InfoWars, the site that is run by notorious conspiracy theorist Alex Jones.
sentences.zh: 讽刺媒体《洋葱报》将接管“电台战争”（InfoWars），一个由臭名昭着的阴谋论者亚历克斯·琼斯运营的网站。

sentences.en: Yes, you heard that correctly.
sentences.zh: 是的，你没听错。

sentences.en: Last Thursday, The Onion launched its own version of InfoWars, the infamous online hub of misinformation created by Alex Jones.
sentences.zh: 上周四，《洋葱报》推出了自己的“电台战争”版本，即由亚历克斯·琼斯创建的那个臭名昭着的在线虚假信息中心。

sentences.en: The takeover has been years in the making.
sentences.zh: 这次接管筹备了多年。

sentences.en: American conspiracy theorist and internet broadcaster Alex Jones has been ordered to pay Sandy Hook families more than one and a half billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 美国阴谋论者和网络广播员亚历克斯·琼斯被命令向桑迪·胡克小学的家属支付超过15亿美元。

sentences.en: That's because he perpetrated for years the lie that this shooting was a hoax, that the people were actors.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他多年来一直在散布谎言，称这次枪击事件是一场骗局，里面的人都是演员。

sentences.en: After losing two defamation cases, Jones was ordered to pay more than a billion dollars to the families affected by the Sandy Hook school shooting.
sentences.zh: 在输掉两起诽谤案后，琼斯被命令向受桑迪·胡克校园枪击案影响的家庭赔偿超过十亿美元。

sentences.en: Breaking news tonight, Alex Jones has just moved to liquidate his personal assets to pay the families of the victims of the Sandy Hook massacre.
sentences.zh: 今晚突发新闻，亚历克斯·琼斯刚刚开始变卖个人资产，以赔偿桑迪·胡克大屠杀受害者的家属。

sentences.en: Unable to pay, Jones' assets, including InfoWars, were put up for auction.
sentences.zh: 由于无力支付，琼斯的资产（包括“电台战争”）被公开拍卖。

sentences.en: He's no longer going to own InfoWars, which is this conspiracy empire he's really used to poison the public discourse.
sentences.zh: 他将不再拥有“电台战争”，这是一个他实际上用来毒害公众舆论的阴谋帝国。

sentences.en: And then, in the surprise twiSt...
sentences.zh: 然后，在一个意想不到的转折中……

sentences.en: The Onion, the satirical news outlet, has won a bankruptcy auction to take control of InfoWars.
sentences.zh: 讽刺新闻媒体《洋葱报》赢得了破产拍卖，取得了“电台战争”的控制权。

sentences.en: The Onion stepped in.
sentences.zh: 《洋葱报》介入了。

sentences.en: They announced plans to convert InfoWars into a parody of itself and committed to sharing proceeds from the new venture with the Sandy Hook families.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布计划将“电台战争”改造成它自身的讽刺版本，并承诺将新创企业的收益与桑迪·胡克小学的家属分享。

sentences.en: Hi everybody, it's Tim Heidecker here.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是蒂姆·海德克。

sentences.en: I'm broadcasting now live.
sentences.zh: 我现在正在进行现场直播。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 感谢收看。

sentences.en: We have major, major announcements to go through here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有重大、重大的公告要宣布。

sentences.en: Now, after nearly two years, the Onion parody of InfoWars is live.
sentences.zh: 现在，经过近两年的时间，《洋葱报》对“电台战争”的讽刺版终于上线了。

sentences.en: Make no mistake, we will be the new InfoWars.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们将成为全新的“电台战争”。

sentences.en: Today, we speak with Onion CEO Ben Collins and comedian Tim Heidecker about what they plan to do with InfoWars and why they fought so hard to take control of it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们与《洋葱报》首席执行官本·柯林斯和喜剧演员蒂姆·海德克一起探讨他们对“电台战争”的计划以及他们为何如此努力地争取其控制权。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, July 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月7日，星期二。

sentences.en: Hi Ben.
sentences.zh: 嗨，本。

sentences.en: Hey, how's it going?
sentences.zh: 嘿，最近怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是蕾切尔·亚当斯。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you too.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Thanks for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你能来。

sentences.en: Thanks for doing this at all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你做这一切。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Early last week, I sat down with Ben Collins, the CEO of The Onion.
sentences.zh: 上周早些时候，我采访了《洋葱报》首席执行官本·柯林斯。

sentences.en: I gotta practice my daily...
sentences.zh: 我得练习一下我的日常……

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: An actor and comedian, Tim Heidecker.
sentences.zh: 演员兼喜剧演员，蒂姆·海德克。

sentences.en: Tim, am I allowed to ask you to just give me your Alex Jones impression?
sentences.zh: 蒂姆，我能请你模仿一下亚历克斯·琼斯吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm like a trained SEAL now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就像一个受过训练的海豹突击队员。

sentences.en: We knew that was the case.
sentences.zh: 我们知道会是这样。

sentences.en: And frankly, that's why we're talking about it, you know.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这就是我们谈论它的原因，你知道的。

sentences.en: Collins and Heidecker were preparing for The Onion's imminent relaunch of InfoWars.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯和海德克正在为《洋葱报》即将重新推出“电台战争”做准备。

sentences.en: The Onion has been around for almost 40 years and became infamous for skewering everything from American politics to pop culture.
sentences.zh: 《洋葱报》已经存在了近40年，以嘲讽从美国政治到流行文化的方方面面而臭名昭著。

sentences.en: In a lot of cases, people need catharsis.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，人们需要宣泄。

sentences.en: Just like give people a, oh, you're not nuts.
sentences.zh: 就像给人们一种，哦，你没疯的感觉。

sentences.en: This feeling of like, you're just not insane.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉就像，你只是没有失去理智。

sentences.en: The shit that's going on is insane, but you're not nuts.
sentences.zh: 正在发生的破事太疯狂了，但你并没有疯。

sentences.en: Collins, who became CEO in 2024 after a decade as a reporter, has revitalized The Onion in a short amount of time.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯在担任了十年记者后于2024年成为首席执行官，他在短时间内重振了《洋葱报》。

sentences.en: And we've leaned into that as hard as we can.
sentences.zh: 我们已经尽最大努力靠向了这一点。

sentences.en: That's why we're the, I think, fifth biggest newspaper in the United States now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为我们现在是美国第五大报纸。

sentences.en: I started my conversation with Ben and Tim by asking why they decided to remake InfoWars.
sentences.zh: 我和本以及蒂姆的对话开始于我询问他们为什么决定重建“电台战争”。

sentences.en: You know, I used to be a reporter, and I was covering stupid stuff on the internet when I was a little wee baby reporter guy at the Daily Beast now, 11 years ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我以前是一名记者，11年前我在《每日野兽》当菜鸟记者的时候，就在互联网上报道各种蠢事。

sentences.en: And my friend's girlfriend was shot and killed on live TV, on Facebook, actually.
sentences.zh: 我朋友的女友在直播中，实际上是在Facebook上被枪杀的。

sentences.en: She was the first person killed by a guy wearing a GoPro.
sentences.zh: 她是第一个被戴着GoPro的人杀死的人。

sentences.en: It was brutal.
sentences.zh: 这太残酷了。

sentences.en: It was just really bad.
sentences.zh: 这真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: And then, like, when you Googled my friend's name, the thing that would come up was that he wasn't real or didn't exist and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你在谷歌上搜索我朋友的名字时，跳出来的东西竟然是他不是真的或者根本不存在之类的话。

sentences.en: Like, there was, the internet had just started to show the cracks of where we were headed.
sentences.zh: 就像是，互联网才刚刚开始暴露出我们正走向何方的裂痕。

sentences.en: So I started covering that for a living.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始以报道这个为生。

sentences.en: You know, I wound up covering Alex Jones' trial in NBC News.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我最后在全国广播公司新闻频道（NBC News）报道了亚历克斯·琼斯的审判。

sentences.en: And I remember sitting there when the judgment came down.
sentences.zh: 我记得判决下来时我坐在那里。

sentences.en: It became clear that he was going to have to owe these people a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他将不得不欠这些人十亿美元。

sentences.en: And he said, I'm not paying any of this.
sentences.zh: 他说，我才不付这笔钱。

sentences.en: You guys know you're not going to receive a penny of this.
sentences.zh: 你们知道你们一分钱也拿不到。

sentences.en: And I was like, hey, dude, I think you've got to pay money.
sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，老兄，我想你必须付钱。

sentences.en: Even after I got this gig, I didn't quite know about all the details.
sentences.zh: 甚至在我得到这份工作后，我还是不太了解所有的细节。

sentences.en: And there's a great documentary about it, The Truth vs. Alex Jones.
sentences.zh: 关于这个有一部很棒的纪录片，《真相对决亚历克斯·琼斯》。

sentences.en: And I sat there, watched that, and just my blood boiled.
sentences.zh: 我坐在那里看完了，简直怒火中烧。

sentences.en: I couldn't believe what he had subjected those poor people to.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信他对那些可怜的人做了什么。

sentences.en: Which we know, of course, he not only accused the Sandy Hook shooting of being fake, he accused the parents of being actors.
sentences.zh: 我们当然知道，他不仅指控桑迪·胡克枪击案是假的，还指控这些父母是演员。

sentences.en: His listeners harassed them.
sentences.zh: 他的听众骚扰了他们。

sentences.en: Some of them had to move.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人不得不搬家。

sentences.en: Alex Jones, as we know, was ordered to pay more than $1.4 billion in damages.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，亚历克斯·琼斯被命令支付超过14亿美元的损害赔偿金。

sentences.en: His assets go to bankruptcy because he does not have that money.
sentences.zh: 他的资产进入破产程序，因为他没有这笔钱。

sentences.en: Can you just, Ben, tell us what happens after that, vis-a-vis your interest in The Onion?
sentences.zh: 本，你能告诉我们之后发生了什么吗，关于你对《洋葱报》的兴趣？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: We saw it was for sale in Forrest on, like, Blue Sky.
sentences.zh: 我们在诸如Blue Sky之类的平台上看到它在拍卖。

sentences.en: There was somebody that clipped out a newspaper ad.
sentences.zh: 有人剪下了一则报纸广告。

sentences.en: Because you have to advertise a bankruptcy auction, which sounds weird.
sentences.zh: 因为你必须为破产拍卖做广告，这听起来很奇怪。

sentences.en: But it said, like, you know, get Alex Jones' armored truck or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但上面写着，你知道的，买下亚历克斯·琼斯的装甲车什么的。

sentences.en: So I started making some phone calls, and I was like, does this mean InfoWars is for sale?
sentences.zh: 所以我开始打一些电话，我在想，“电台战争”是在拍卖吗？

sentences.en: And they were like, yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 他们说，是的，是的。

sentences.en: You get the IP if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要的话，你可以得到知识产权。

sentences.en: And I just tried to figure out what to do.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想该做些什么。

sentences.en: Because I had obviously never purchased something at a bankruptcy auction.
sentences.zh: 因为我显然从未在破产拍卖中买过东西。

sentences.en: So I had to, like, learn some stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不去学习一些东西。

sentences.en: And we were like, okay, well, we can look at this.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，好吧，我们可以看看这个。

sentences.en: And I think we can pull this off.
sentences.zh: 我想我们能搞定。

sentences.en: So we get excited to bid on this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很高兴能对这个东西进行竞标。

sentences.en: And the bidding is on, I think, November 14th of 2024.
sentences.zh: 竞标大约在2024年11月14日进行。

sentences.en: And what happens on November 5th of 2024 is Donald Trump is elected president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 而在2024年11月5日发生的事情是唐纳德·特朗普当选美国总统。

sentences.en: So people are wondering, like, should we do this?
sentences.zh: 所以人们在想，我们应该这样做吗？

sentences.en: Is this a safe thing to do?
sentences.zh: 这样做安全吗？

sentences.en: Dan Bongino, who became the deputy director of the FBI, got his start in InfoWars.
sentences.zh: 后来成为联邦调查局（FBI）副局长的丹·邦吉诺就是从“电台战争”起家的。

sentences.en: There were so many people tied up in those worlds.
sentences.zh: 有那么多人都与那些世界纠缠在一起。

sentences.en: So people were spooked.
sentences.zh: 所以人们都吓坏了。

sentences.en: And we just had to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不做出决定。

sentences.en: And I just realized that I can't imagine other people had the gumption or just, like, time in their lives to take on Alex Jones's harassment campaign.
sentences.zh: 我只是意识到，我无法想象其他人有勇气或者有生之年有时间去承担亚历克斯·琼斯的骚扰活动。

sentences.en: So I was like, okay, you know, I'm mad at my word.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，好吧，你知道的，我一言既出。

sentences.en: We're going to go through this.
sentences.zh: 我们要坚持到底。

sentences.en: And we put down her bid.
sentences.zh: 我们提交了出价。

sentences.en: And then we won.
sentences.zh: 然后我们赢了。

sentences.en: And then Alex absolutely lost his mind.
sentences.zh: 接着亚历克斯彻底疯了。

sentences.en: I remember him calling Steve Bannon on air and being like, Steve Bannon being like, what the fuck is going on?
sentences.zh: 我记得他在节目中打电话给史蒂夫·班农，史蒂夫·班农当时说：“这他妈是怎么回事？”

sentences.en: Like, on the phone, on air, on the floor, as it was, like, he was panicking.
sentences.zh: 就像在电话里、在节目直播中、在现场那样，他当时惊慌失措。

sentences.en: The funniest part is he had never heard of The Onion until he bought it.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是，在买下它之前，他甚至没听说过《洋葱报》。

sentences.en: You're kidding.
sentences.zh: 你在开玩笑吧。

sentences.en: He said that?
sentences.zh: 他这么说过？

sentences.en: Well, you could tell.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看得出来。

sentences.en: Like, he was like, this newspaper, The Onion.
sentences.zh: 就像他说的那样，这份报纸，《洋葱报》。

sentences.en: And he just never heard of it.
sentences.zh: 他只是从没听说过它。

sentences.en: Just to clarify here.
sentences.zh: 这里澄清一下。

sentences.en: So basically, the point of the bankruptcy is that whatever gets sold, everything's supposed to go to the families that got that judgment, right?
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，破产的意义在于，无论卖出什么，所有东西都应该归于获得该判决的家属，对吧？

sentences.en: So at this point, when you were trying to purchase his assets, his company, was the idea to take it over and give money to the families in some way?
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时候，当你试图购买他的资产、他的公司时，你的想法是接管它并以某种方式把钱给这些家庭吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that was the immediate argument when I presented it to my team.
sentences.zh: 是的，当我把这个方案呈交给我的团队时，这就是最直接的论点。

sentences.en: I was like, you know, we could spend $2 million on Facebook ads and make $2.1 million in Onion merch or something.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，我们可以在Facebook广告上花200万美元，然后通过《洋葱报》的周边商品赚取210万美元之类的。

sentences.en: Or we can do this really good thing and hope people come along for the ride.
sentences.zh: 或者我们可以做这件真正的好事，并希望人们能加入进来。

sentences.en: And that's what we decided to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们决定要做的事。

sentences.en: And we, look, we, I have no idea if I would do it again, but I think I would because it's been this gigantic pain in the ass in my life.
sentences.zh: 听着，我不知道我是否还会再做一次，但我想我会的，因为它成了我生命中一个巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: And it's been very scary.
sentences.zh: 而且这非常吓人。

sentences.en: And we've had the dogs called on us from him and all of his weird psycho.
sentences.zh: 他和他的那些怪异精神病患者甚至报警找人来对付我们。

sentences.en: Alex Jones has come after both of you personally, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我相信亚历克斯·琼斯亲自找过你们两个的麻烦。

sentences.en: Oh, in the best possible way.
sentences.zh: 哦，以最好的方式。

sentences.en: I find it incredibly amusing for the most part.
sentences.zh: 大部分时间我都觉得这极其滑稽。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because he's discovered my body of work.
sentences.zh: 因为他发现了我的作品。

sentences.en: Like you say, he didn't know The Onion.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他以前不认识《洋葱报》。

sentences.en: And then he found Tim and Eric's stuff from 15 years ago.
sentences.zh: 然后他发现了蒂姆和埃里克15年前的东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you haven't seen some of that, it is pretty out there.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你没看过其中一些内容，那确实挺离谱的。

sentences.en: It's pretty weird.
sentences.zh: 相当怪异。

sentences.en: But it's all coming from a place of absurdity and a place of silliness.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都源于荒诞和滑稽。

sentences.en: But he took it all out of context and basically thought that we were some kind of literal demons from hell.
sentences.zh: 但他断章取义，基本上把我们当成了某种来自地狱的字面意义上的恶魔。

sentences.en: So you make a bid for The Onion.
sentences.zh: 所以你为《洋葱报》出价。

sentences.en: It goes through some legal wrangling in the courts.
sentences.zh: 它经历了一些法庭上的法律争端。

sentences.en: Now you have, I believe, celebrated the takeover.
sentences.zh: 现在我想你们已经庆祝了这次接管。

sentences.en: I know that you guys are treating it like a fait accompli you're about to launch.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们把它当作既成事实，马上就要启动了。

sentences.en: But what is the current status?
sentences.zh: 但目前的现状是怎样的？

sentences.en: Just to be clear, like you have not officially taken over in the sense that like you can't go into Alex Jones's studio right now in Austin and like start broadcasting from there.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，你们并没有正式接管，也就是说你们现在还不能走进亚历克斯·琼斯在奥斯汀的工作室然后从那里开始广播。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So last August, there was an emergency stay put in place where it says like the receiver cannot sell these assets until we rule on this.
sentences.zh: 所以在去年8月，有一个紧急暂缓令生效，上面说破产管理人不能出售这些资产，直到我们对此做出裁决。

sentences.en: The receiver is the guy in charge of dispensing all of these assets.
sentences.zh: 破产管理人是负责处理所有这些资产的人。

sentences.en: And then Alex Jones said that he was going to shut everything down.
sentences.zh: 然后亚历克斯·琼斯说他要关掉一切。

sentences.en: Alex Jones's goal, by the way, is to render these assets valueless so he can buy them back for pennies.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，亚历克斯·琼斯的目标是让这些资产变得毫无价值，这样他就可以用极低的价格把它们买回来。

sentences.en: I don't accept that because that means these families will never get anything.
sentences.zh: 我不能接受这一点，因为这意味着这些家庭将永远一无所获。

sentences.en: So we went to this receiver and we said, we'll lease all of this stuff from you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们找到了这位破产管理人，并对他说，我们从你这里租下所有这些东西。

sentences.en: I know you can't sell it, but it doesn't say anything about this.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们不能卖它，但这里面可没提这个。

sentences.en: And the receiver is like, yeah, I guess that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 然后接盘方就说，好吧，我觉得这倒是个好主意。

sentences.en: My goal is to keep the value of the assets up and make the families happy.
sentences.zh: 我的目标是保住资产价值，并让那些家庭感到快乐。

sentences.en: And so we're moving this forward.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在推进这件事。

sentences.en: And part of why we're trying to do this is to keep the value of this asset alive.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以要这么做，部分原因也是为了让这笔资产的价值存续下去。

sentences.en: By making fun of this thing, we were reminding people like, hey, it has value on the planet Earth and has value to us.
sentences.zh: 通过对这玩意儿进行群嘲，我们在提醒大家，嘿，它在地球上有价值，对我们也有价值。

sentences.en: And, you know, we would love to take this over and give these families.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们很乐意把它接手过来并交还给这些家庭。

sentences.en: They haven't received a penny from this guy.
sentences.zh: 他们连这家伙的一分钱都没拿到。

sentences.en: And it's been four and a half years since the judgment and 10 years since they sued him.
sentences.zh: 距离判决已经过去四年半了，距离他们起诉他也已经10年了。

sentences.en: So they need this cash and we would love to get them some.
sentences.zh: 所以他们急需这笔现金，而我们很乐意帮他们搞到一些。

sentences.en: How did the families react when you first told them that you wanted to take this horrific tragedy and make it into a comedy website?
sentences.zh: 当你第一次告诉这些家庭，你想把这场可怕的悲剧变成一个喜剧网站时，他们的反应是什么？

sentences.en: The first call was weird because I was like, I work at The Onion.
sentences.zh: 第一通电话挺诡异的，因为我说，我在《洋葱报》工作。

sentences.en: I used to cover this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我以前报道过这些事。

sentences.en: So a couple of these families knew who I was.
sentences.zh: 所以其中好几个家庭知道我是谁。

sentences.en: And they were like, let me think about it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就说，让我想想看。

sentences.en: And then they came back and they were like, now that I thought about it, I see the vision, you know, because their goal has always been, you know,
sentences.zh: 接着他们回电话说，我现在想通了，我懂你们的宏图，你知道的，因为他们的目标一直都是，你知道的，

sentences.en: make it so he can't do this to any other family ever again.
sentences.zh: 让他再也无法对任何其他家庭做出这种事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: This, like, double whammy of American life that is you just lost your kids in a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 美国生活中的这种双重打击，也就是你在悲剧失去了孩子。

sentences.en: And now I'm going to tell everybody they never really lived or they're still alive and they graduated from high school.
sentences.zh: 而现在我要告诉所有人，他们根本没活过，或者他们还活着而且高中毕业了。

sentences.en: That's a thing that these people say now.
sentences.zh: 现在这帮人居然会说这种话。

sentences.en: And I – the strength of these families is absurd.
sentences.zh: 而我——这些家庭展现出的坚韧简直不可思议。

sentences.en: Like, you've met these people.
sentences.zh: 就像你见过的这些人一样。

sentences.en: They are the strongest people I think I've ever met in my entire life.
sentences.zh: 他们是我这辈子见过的最坚强的人。

sentences.en: And then we had this, like, really beautiful phone call with them maybe a month ago where –
sentences.zh: 然后我们大约在一个月前和他们打了一通非常美好的电话，当时——

sentences.en: The two of you.
sentences.zh: 你们两个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It was us and the Onion writing staff.
sentences.zh: 是我们和《洋葱报》的编辑团队。

sentences.en: Yeah, everybody.
sentences.zh: 对，所有人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then I think, like, six or seven of the families.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，大概有六七个家庭吧。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And – I don't know.
sentences.zh: 然后——我不知道。

sentences.en: A bunch of people left overtly crying in the office.
sentences.zh: 办公室里有好几个人直接哭着离开了。

sentences.en: It was weird to go into a thing where we thought we were going to say thank you for letting us do this.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉很奇妙，我们本来以为去那是为了说谢谢你们让我们做这件事。

sentences.en: And they were like, no, no, no, no, I don't think you're going to understand.
sentences.zh: 而他们却说，不不不不，我觉得你们没搞懂。

sentences.en: Thank you for doing this.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们来做这件事。

sentences.en: But I want to go back to this idea that one of the reasons the family supported you and one of your goals is to neuter Alex Jones.
sentences.zh: 但我还想回到这个观点，即家庭支持你的原因之一，以及你的目标之一，就是阉割亚历克斯·琼斯。

sentences.en: Because Alex Jones, he might not have InfoWars, but he is up and running on the platform Rumble.
sentences.zh: 因为亚历克斯·琼斯，他可能没有了InfoWars，但他在Rumble平台上依然活得好好的。

sentences.en: He is doing his thing.
sentences.zh: 他还在干他的老本行。

sentences.en: He still has people that are watching him.
sentences.zh: 他依然有拥趸在看他。

sentences.en: It is nowhere near the millions of people he had on YouTube before he was kicked off of YouTube.
sentences.zh: 这和他在被油管封禁之前在油管上拥有的数百万粉丝相比，简直九牛一毛。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, he is starting to do the same thing he's done before, right?
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，他开始重操旧业了，对吧？

sentences.en: And we don't know how big he's going to be.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不知道他能壮大到什么程度。

sentences.en: So I just sort of wonder, like, if he's already out there, like, still doing his thing, like, what – how will you determine whether this effort is successful?
sentences.zh: 所以我只是在想，如果他已经重出江湖，还在老调重弹，那么——你将如何评判这项努力是否成功？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I tuned in the other day just because I hadn't done the impression in a while and I wanted to listen to his voice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，前几天我还特意调过去看了一眼，纯粹是因为我有一阵没模仿他了，想听听他的声音。

sentences.en: And I literally opened it up and he was talking about Charlie Kirk faking his own death.
sentences.zh: 结果我一打开，他就正在讨论查理·柯克假死的事。

sentences.en: I was like, right.
sentences.zh: 我就想，果然如此。

sentences.en: And we're doing a little bit of a similar take on that, on our parody of it.
sentences.zh: 而我们也在我们的恶搞中对这一现象进行了类似的讽刺。

sentences.en: I mean, he is extremely diminished from where he was six years ago, ten years ago.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，和六年前、十年前相比，他现在的影响力已经极度萎缩了。

sentences.en: It has, like, 6,000 views per stream.
sentences.zh: 现在每次直播大概只有6000次观看。

sentences.en: Like, this is not –
sentences.zh: 就像，这根本——

sentences.en: It's small.
sentences.zh: 规模很小。

sentences.en: It's small.
sentences.zh: 规模很小。

sentences.en: It's a small audience.
sentences.zh: 受众很少。

sentences.en: And I agree with you that he can build it back up, but that's America.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的看法，他确实有可能东山再起，但这就是美国。

sentences.en: We should also note that the core of Alex Jones is a pills-selling machine.
sentences.zh: 我们还应该指出，亚历克斯·琼斯的核心本质是一台卖药机器。

sentences.en: It is –
Well, just to be really clear about what you mean here is that he has a part of his business where he sells products to people.
sentences.zh: 好吧，为了把你的意思解释清楚，他的业务中有一部分是向人们推销产品。

sentences.en: And in some cases, those products are to solve issues that he brings up on his show that might not be actual evidence-based issues or solutions.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，这些产品是为了解决他在节目中提出的一些问题，而这些问题可能并不是真正有据可查的问题或解决方案。

sentences.en: A nuclear war is imminent, therefore, by my iodine.
sentences.zh: 核战争迫在眉睫，因此，快买我的碘片。

sentences.en: Stuff like that, right.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类，对吧。

sentences.en: I also just have to point out, did you guys see – I think it was New York Magazine, but I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我还不得不指出，你们看到过吗——我觉得好像是《纽约杂志》，但我记不清了。

sentences.en: Somebody years ago did a quiz.
sentences.zh: 几年前有人出过一个小测验。

sentences.en: Is this product from Alex Jones or is this product from Gwyneth Paltrow?
sentences.zh: 这个产品是亚历克斯·琼斯的，还是格温妮丝·帕特洛的？

sentences.en: Right, sure.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: And it was very hard to tell the difference, so you don't want to make it seem like it's singular to Alex Jones.
sentences.zh: 而且根本很难分辨，所以你可不想让人觉得这是亚历克斯·琼斯独有的套路。

sentences.en: No, no, but I mean she's not advocating for the harassment of parents.
sentences.zh: 不，不，但我的意思是她并没有煽动去骚扰父母。

sentences.en: I think that's the difference is you can do whatever you want to sell products.
sentences.zh: 我觉得区别就在于，你可以为了卖货做任何你想做的事。

sentences.en: Once you start selling products on – as a direct response immediately after a mass shooting and start demeaning the people who are victims of that mass shooting, that's – to me,
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始在——作为大规模枪击事件发生后的直接连续反应开始兜售产品，并开始贬低那些遭遇大规模枪击事件的受害者时，在我看来，

sentences.en: I don't know if I'm crazy here, is a step too far.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是不是我疯了，但这绝对是太过分了。

sentences.en: The two of you have done a very good job of articulating, I think, what you think the core of Alex Jones' product empire and also website is.
sentences.zh: 你们两个把你们认为的亚历克斯·琼斯的产品帝国以及网站的核心阐述得非常到位。

sentences.en: You've also explained a lot about the onion and what sort of makes the onion the onion.
sentences.zh: 你们也对《洋葱报》以及究竟是什么造就了《洋葱报》做出了很多解释。

sentences.en: Can you help me understand how does InfoWars fit into the core DNA of the onion?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我理解一下，InfoWars是怎么契合《洋葱报》的核心DNA的吗？

sentences.en: So the onion, in my opinion, has always been the best at going after the dominant mode of media at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以在我的观点里，《洋葱报》一直以来都是狙击当时主流媒体模式最强的存在。

sentences.en: We always go after the way people actually get their information.
sentences.zh: 我们总是针对人们实际获取信息的方式下手。

sentences.en: And this was a shot across the bow.
sentences.zh: 而这可以说是当头棒喝。

sentences.en: It's a little bit bigger than what we usually do in the sense that we're directly going after the information war people who are trying to make you feel bad about everything you do so you can buy a supplement.
sentences.zh: 它比我们平时的常规操作要宏大一些，因为我们是直接冲着那些“信息战”贩子去的，他们试图让你对你做的每件事都感到内疚，好让你去买他们的保健品。

sentences.en: But that's how everything operates.
sentences.zh: 但现在的万物运作不都是这样吗？

sentences.en: You see like RFK who is carrying around sauerkraut and talking about peptides and all these other things like the current du jour addiction of people who subscribe to things on the internet.
sentences.zh: 你看像小肯尼迪，整天带着酸菜到处跑，谈论多肽以及所有这些其他东西，就像现在网民们的流行时尚迷恋一样。

sentences.en: So like to me, it was an obvious opportunity to take this model that was invented, like really not invented, but perfected by Alex Jones and say, let's just lay it all bare.
sentences.zh: 所以对我和说，这是一个显而易见的机会，可以把这种模式——这种由亚历克斯·琼斯发明，好吧，其实不是发明，但被他发扬光大的模式拿过来，说一句，让我们把它扒个精光。

sentences.en: After the break, we talk about what it is like to make comedy in this political environment.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，我们来聊聊在这种政治环境下做喜剧是怎样一种体验。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年历史的老物件。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听由爱彼呈现的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 因为我实在不爱洗平底锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，持续助您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即访问nytimes.com/subscribe订阅，尊享特惠。

sentences.en: I want to talk about comedy, not just InfoWars comedy, but just sort of more broadly comedy in the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 我想聊聊喜剧，不仅仅是InfoWars式的喜剧，而是更广泛意义上的特朗普政府时期的喜剧。

sentences.en: A lot of comedians have said, and I've heard you guys discuss this, that satire is really hard in the Trump administration, which is I've never quite understood exactly why.
sentences.zh: 很多喜剧演员都说过，我也听你们讨论过，在特朗普政府时期做讽刺真的很难，这一点我一直不太明白为什么。

sentences.en: And I feel like it's not the perspective that you guys have taken.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这并不是你们所采取的视角。

sentences.en: And so I wonder if, Tim, you can explain what you think the opportunity is for comedy that other comedians who say that are missing.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，蒂姆，你能否解释一下，你认为其他喜剧演员所忽视的喜剧机遇究竟是什么？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, you try to get to very universal, you know, human feelings.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你得去触及非常普世的，你知道的，人类的情感。

sentences.en: I'm not trying to just go like, ha ha, look at Trump's orange complexion.
sentences.zh: 我可不想只是去搞那种，哈哈，你看特朗普那张橘子脸。

sentences.en: I want to get into like, what is it about being a human being that gets you to the place where you're doing that to yourself?
sentences.zh: 我想深入探讨的是，究竟是人类的什么特质，才会让你把自己搞成那样？

sentences.en: And I want to try to do that in an entertaining or funny way.
sentences.zh: 而且我想以一种娱乐或搞笑的方式来做到这一点。

sentences.en: I think it's also okay to, at this moment in time, it's enough to just go, like whatever the debacle is this week, whatever the insanity is, I think it's enough right now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在当下的时间节点，这样做也没问题：只要抛出本周的闹剧是什么，无论有多疯狂，我觉得现在这就足够了。

sentences.en: You can just go, I think that's crazy.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接说，我觉得这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And if you can try to do it in a funny, witty way, at least people out there looking for signals that they're not alone can get something.
sentences.zh: 如果你能试着用一种滑稽、机智的方式把它表达出来，至少那些在寻找自己并不孤单的信号的人们能从中获得点什么。

sentences.en: They can get like, okay, I'm not crazy.
sentences.zh: 他们能得到这样的安慰：好吧，我没疯。

sentences.en: That's crazy.
sentences.zh: 这群人才疯了。

sentences.en: I want to ask you guys, though, like the way you are describing what you're doing does not sound ideological.
sentences.zh: 不过我想问你们，你们描述自己所做事情的方式听起来并不带有意识形态色彩。

sentences.en: But just to push back a little bit, like I went to the Onion website earlier today and there's like a zillion headlines about Trump and RFK Jr., Ken Paxton.
sentences.zh: 但为了稍微反驳一下，比如我今天早些时候去了《洋葱报》的网站，上面有成吨关于特朗普、小罗伯特·肯尼迪、肯·帕克斯顿的头条新闻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I'm somebody who's read The Onion.
sentences.zh: 而且我是一个读过《洋葱报》的人。

sentences.en: I know that you made fun of Biden.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们开过拜登的玩笑。

sentences.en: I know that you make fun of Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们拿民主党人开涮。

sentences.en: I get that.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: But there's something called the Babylon Bee, which for people that don't know, it is very funny stuff.
sentences.zh: 但有个东西叫“巴比伦蜜蜂”，对于不了解的人来说，那上面的东西非常搞笑。

sentences.en: It is described as like the onion for conservatives, basically the implication being that you guys have a liberal ideological bent.
sentences.zh: 它被描述为什么保守派的《洋葱报》，其潜台词基本上就是你们带有自由派的意识形态倾向。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that certainly in this moment, you could get that impression looking at The Onion website.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在这个时刻，浏览《洋葱报》的网站确实会给人留下这种印象。

sentences.en: I want to understand, like, how broad are you trying to appeal in terms of an audience?
sentences.zh: 我想了解的是，就受众群体而言，你们的受众定位究竟有多广？

sentences.en: I would just say that I don't think about an audience often.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，我通常不会去考虑受众是谁。

sentences.en: I just try to express what's inside of me out into the world.
sentences.zh: 我只是试图把内心的想法表达并传递到世界上。

sentences.en: And it will be ideological a lot of the time because I have a point of view.
sentences.zh: 很多时候它确实会带有一种意识形态色彩，因为我有自己的观点。

sentences.en: But I will say Infowars isn't going to be overtly political necessarily and maybe not really at all.
sentences.zh: 但我得说，Infowars不一定会带有显而易见的政治色彩，甚至可能根本没有。

sentences.en: I mean, we're making fun of food influencers and we'll be making fun of people that certainly voted for, you know, Mamdani in New York, you know, and are friends of mine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在取笑美食网红，我们也会取笑那些在纽约投票给曼达尼的人，你知道的，他们还是我的朋友。

sentences.en: Like, you've got to, of course, look at the world around you and see things that you kind of cringe at, even though you might ideologically align with them.
sentences.zh: 比如，你必须审视身边的世界，看到那些让你感到尴尬的事情，哪怕你在意识形态上与他们保持一致。

sentences.en: And we're not going to be afraid to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会害怕去这样做。

sentences.en: But we're not interested in punching down.
sentences.zh: 但我们对向下欺凌毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: We're not looking at making fun of swaths of people because we're essentially scared of them.
sentences.zh: 我们不会因为内心对某些人群感到恐惧而去嘲笑他们。

sentences.en: Yeah, the most recent takedown request we got from a politician was from a very prominent Democrat.
sentences.zh: 对，我们最近收到的一份来自政客的撤稿请求就来自于一位非常显赫的民主党人。

sentences.en: You know, that's we really do hammer all sides.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们确实是各打五十大板。

sentences.en: The Democratic Party is really upset at us because they think that we sank Joe Biden's 2024 campaign.
sentences.zh: 民主党对我们非常愤怒，因为他们觉得是我们搞砸了乔·拜登2024年的竞选。

sentences.en: Because you didn't cheer him on.
sentences.zh: 因为你们没有为他摇旗呐喊。

sentences.en: Is that the idea?
sentences.zh: 是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to ever step in on that sort of thing ever.
sentences.zh: 而我绝不会在这类事情上妥协。

sentences.en: I wonder if you guys succeed, if the website takes off, besides the financial benefit of succeeding, whatever that looks like, whatever your metrics are,
sentences.zh: 我在想，如果你们成功了，如果这个网站真的火了，除了成功的财务收益（无论它表现为什么样，无论你们的衡量标准是什么），

sentences.en: just what do you think you will have accomplished besides sidelining Alex Jones, besides making him less offensive or powerful?
sentences.zh: 除了边缘化亚历克斯·琼斯、除了削弱他的冒犯性或影响力之外，你们觉得你们还达成了什么成就？

sentences.en: I mean, creating another place for quality art and media to exist that is pretty damn independent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，创造了另一个高质量艺术和媒体能够生存的空间，而且相当独立。

sentences.en: I mean, this is one of the few bastions of not this monopolized super companies that we're having to live with.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我们不得不忍受的那些被垄断的超级大公司之外，为数不多的堡垒之一。

sentences.en: So what we hope to have accomplished in, let's say,
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望在，比方说，

sentences.en: five years is we've retrained people's brains to think of Infowars meaning something fundamentally different and separate it from that ghoul.
sentences.zh: 五年里取得的成就是，我们重塑了人们大脑中的认知，让Infowars代表着截然不同的全新含义，并把它和那个恶魔彻底切割开来。

sentences.en: If he wants to tell people about Charlie Kirk faking his own death or something, he's free to do it on the side of the highway.
sentences.zh: 如果他想跟别人讲查理·柯克假死之类的事，他大可以在高速公路边随便讲。

sentences.en: You know, everything about Infowars was horrible, except the branding and the catchphrase they came up with.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，Infowars的一切都糟糕透顶，除了它的品牌塑造和他们想出来的那个标语。

sentences.en: And their catchphrase is there's a war on for your mind, which is just a perfect sentence.
sentences.zh: 而他们的标语是“有一场针对你思想的战争”，这简直是一句完美的话。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful sentence, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一句绝妙的话，对吧？

sentences.en: And that will remain a thing that we do, basically like a mission statement or, you know, something to point at where there has been a war on for your mind for the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这将继续成为我们会做的事情，基本上就像一个使命宣言，或者，你知道的，一个指向过去的标志：过去10年里确实一直在进行一场针对你思想的战争。

sentences.en: There's no question about that.
sentences.zh: 这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: Like we have lived through that.
sentences.zh: 就像我们都经历过这一切一样。

sentences.en: And I would say normal people have lost in part because they didn't know they were in a fight.
sentences.zh: 而且我想说，普通人的落败，部分原因就在于他们根本不知道自己正身处战场。

sentences.en: And we're going to give people the ability to make fun of the processes and the ways people get information.
sentences.zh: 我们将赋予人们嘲弄各种流程以及人们获取信息方式的能力。

sentences.en: That's going to be the through line that gets us through this.
sentences.zh: 这将是贯穿始终、带我们度过难关的主线。

sentences.en: And like characters and ideas and things are going to build out of that.
sentences.zh: 各种角色、想法以及事物也将在此基础上衍生出来。

sentences.en: We are constantly being inundated with a bunch of insane garbage and bullshit, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦白讲，我们时刻都被大量疯狂的垃圾信息和胡言乱语所淹没。

sentences.en: And that bullshit had no counterweight.
sentences.zh: 而这些胡言乱语没有任何制衡的力量。

sentences.en: And we're going to try to do that to start.
sentences.zh: 我们首先打算做的就是这件事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, yeah, I think the—sorry to interrupt you, but I've been thinking over the years a lot about darkness and comedy and death and comedy.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，对，我认为——抱歉打断你，但我这些年一直在思考很多关于黑暗与喜剧、死亡与喜剧的事情。

sentences.en: And it is a way to, like, survive the chaos of the world.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一种在某种程度上挺过世界混乱的方式。

sentences.en: On a very deep level, like the comedians, the writers, whoever,
sentences.zh: 在一个很深的层面，比如喜剧演员、作家，无论何人，

sentences.en: creatives that go into those dark places are doing it at a service for themselves to sort of exercise the fear of these real things.
sentences.zh: 涉足那些黑暗之地的创意工作者，其实是在为自己服务，以此来排解对这些现实事物的恐惧。

sentences.en: And then that gets received by an audience, and I think it does a service to make them feel like, okay, this is something that happens, and we have to laugh about it.
sentences.zh: 然后这些内容被观众接收，我认为这起到了一种作用，让他们觉得，好吧，这是会发生的事情，我们得笑对它。

sentences.en: There's obviously lots of things we could do about it, but it's just like making you feel like all this crazy shit is hanging over our heads.
sentences.zh: 显然我们对此有很多能做的事，但这就像是让你觉得所有这些疯狂的破事都悬在我们头顶。

sentences.en: But we shouldn't be afraid of it all the time.
sentences.zh: 但我们不应该一直对此感到恐惧。

sentences.en: Ben, Tim, thank you both so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 本、蒂姆，非常感谢两广光临我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: After we spoke to Ben and Tim, we reached out to representatives for Alex Jones, tasked for comment about The Onion's takeover of InfoWars.
sentences.zh: 在与本和蒂姆交谈后，我们联系了亚历克斯·琼斯的代表，要求就《洋葱报》接管 InfoWars 一事置评。

sentences.en: But they did not respond.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有回应。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《构想者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每天晚上都会带着300件你最珍视的藏品去上班，把DJ台变成这样一个，

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 充满活力的、由精美50年历史文物组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听由爱彼呈现的《构想者》。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘wynna。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块字谜游戏 Connections 的创作者，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天创作 Spelling Bee 和 Letterboxd 游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的人这样的一群人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 细分 games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Calls mounted on Monday for the resignation of Graham Plattner, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Maine, after a former girlfriend accused him of rape.
sentences.zh: 周一，各方纷纷呼吁缅因州参议院民主党提名人格雷厄姆·普拉特纳辞职，此前他的前女友指控他强奸。

sentences.en: In an interview with Politico, the former girlfriend, Jenny Rassikot, described an incident during which Plattner let himself into her home and forced himself on her,
sentences.zh: 在前女友珍妮·拉西科特接受 Politico 采访时，她描述了一起事件：普拉特纳擅自闯入她的家中并强暴了她，

sentences.en: despite her repeated pleas for him to stop.
sentences.zh: 尽管她一再恳求他住手。

sentences.en: In a social media post, Plattner denied the allegations and said he would take time to, quote, reflect on the path forward.
sentences.zh: 普拉特纳在社交媒体发文中否认了这些指控，并表示他需要时间来“反思未来的道路”。

sentences.en: Both parties see Maine as a battle in the midterms and a deciding race over who will control the Senate.
sentences.zh: 两党都将缅因州视为中期选举的一场关键战役，也是决定谁将控制参议院的关键竞选。

sentences.en: Prominent Democrats withdrew their endorsements of Plattner after the allegations surfaced on Monday, including Senator Elizabeth Warren, Representative Ro Khanna,
sentences.zh: 在周一指控浮出水面后，多位知名民主党人撤回了对普拉特纳的支持，其中包括参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦、众议员罗·卡纳，

sentences.en: and Senator Ruben Gallego.
sentences.zh: 以及参议员鲁本·加莱戈。

sentences.en: The Senate Democratic campaign arm, which had opposed Plattner in the primary,
sentences.zh: 参议院民主党竞选机构曾在初选中反对普拉特纳，

sentences.en: also called for him to quit and pledged to withhold financial support from his campaign if he remained in the race.
sentences.zh: 如今也呼吁他退选，并承诺如果他继续参选，将扣留对其竞选的资金支持。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Caitlin O'Keefe and Chris Benderev.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由凯特琳·奥基夫和克里斯·本德列夫制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George with help from Ben Calhoun, Michael Benoit, and Paige Cowett, and contains music by Pat McCusker, Alicia Baitoub, and Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 节目由马克·乔治剪辑，并得到了本·卡尔霍恩、迈克尔·贝努瓦和佩吉·考特的帮助，其中包含帕特·麦库斯克、艾莉西亚·拜图布和马里恩·洛扎诺的音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由 Wonderly 创作。

sentences.en: This episode was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由艾莉莎·莫克利担任工程制作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。
